title: "Data"

## Overview

WISE-APP connects to a standardized data directory structured into three primary components: **metadata**, **microdata**, and **hazard** datasets (historical weather and future climate projections). Microdata and hazard layers are spatially linked using the [H3 spatial indexing system](https://h3geo.org), which maps survey locations to hexagonal grid cells shared with gridded climate data.

## Connecting to Data

WISE-APP is designed to query datasets lazily using an in-process **DuckDB** engine, enabling high-performance queries across local or remote cloud storage without downloading entire datasets into memory.

### Web Application (Automatic Connection)

When accessing WISE-APP via the internal web platform ([WISE-APP Online](https://datanalytics-int.worldbank.org/wise-app){target="_blank"}), the data connection is **automatically configured**. The app connects directly to curated Databricks Volumes hosting harmonized GMD surveys, ERA5-Land reanalysis, and CMIP6 climate scenarios. No manual setup or credential entry is required.

### Local R Package (Interactive Connection via Overview Page)

When running the application locally in R, launch the app:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("worldbank/welfare-weather-app")
wiseapp::run_app()
```

On startup, the **Overview** landing page provides an interactive **Data** connection panel allowing you to connect to any supported storage backend:

- **Local folder:** Path to a local directory (defaults to `data/`).
- **Amazon S3:** Bucket name, key prefix, region, and AWS access keys.
- **Google Cloud Storage (GCS):** Bucket name, prefix, and service account JSON.
- **Azure Blob / Data Lake Storage:** Storage account, container name, prefix, and account key or Service Principal credentials.
- **Hugging Face:** Dataset repository, subdirectory, and access token.
- **Databricks:** Workspace URL, Databricks Volume path (`/Volumes/...`), and OAuth M2M credentials.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Analytical Tip: Environment Credentials
Credential fields in the UI are optional if credentials are pre-configured in your local `.Renviron` file (e.g., `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AZURE_STORAGE_KEY`, `DATABRICKS_HOST`, etc.).
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### Data Preparation Repository
The data processing pipelines used to clean, harmonize, and spatially index microdata and hazard layers are maintained in the [welfare-weather-app-data](https://github.com/worldbank/welfare-weather-app-data){target="_blank"} repository.
:::

## Data Sources & Methodology

This section describes the data sources prepared for the web app. 

### Household Survey Microdata (GMD)

Socioeconomic data are drawn from the World Bank’s Global Monitoring Database (GMD), a repository of harmonized multi-topic household surveys. GMD provides standardized consumption aggregates, poverty measures, and demographic indicators across countries and survey rounds.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
### Analytical Caveat: Survey Design & Variance Estimation
While survey sampling weights are applied during reporting to ensure representativeness, GMD does not harmonize full complex survey design parameters (such as primary sampling units, strata, and clusters). Consequently, standard errors estimated by the regression models may be underestimated. The inclusion of spatial fixed effects partially mitigates this issue, but uncertainty intervals should be interpreted with appropriate caution.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
### Analytical Caveat: Spatial & Temporal Granularity
Accurate linking with weather data depends on the precision of interview dates and geolocation. When survey data are anonymized to broad administrative regions (e.g., province or governorate) or coarse time intervals (e.g., quarter of interview), the spatial and temporal variation in weather shocks is smoothed out, reducing statistical power and attenuation toward zero.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
### Analytical Tip: Variable Coverage & Missing Data
Beyond core demographic and consumption variables, the availability of resilience proxies (e.g., electricity access, education, assets) varies across surveys. When using automated selection algorithms like LASSO in Step 1, variables with high missing rates (>10%) are excluded by default. It is strongly recommended to review survey statistics prior to modeling to verify that key variables are not systematically missing for vulnerable sub-populations.
:::

### Historical Weather Reanalysis (ERA5-Land)

Historical weather data are obtained from **ERA5-Land**, a global climate reanalysis produced by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). ERA5-Land combines physical modeling with global in-situ and satellite observations to provide consistent, hourly estimates of meteorological variables at a ~9 km spatial resolution from 1950 to the present.

For WISE-APP, ERA5-Land variables are aggregated to monthly summaries (e.g., mean temperature, precipitation sums, standardized anomalies) and spatially mapped onto H3 hexagonal cells.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
### Analytical Caveat: Local Variation and Fixed Effects Identification
A regression model with spatial and temporal fixed effects identifies weather impacts solely from *within-location* and *within-time* deviations from local baselines. If a country or survey sample exhibits little localized weather variation across interview dates, the model cannot identify meaningful statistical relationships.
:::

### Climate Projections (CMIP6 SSP Scenarios)

Future climate scenarios are sourced from the **Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6)** under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs):

- **SSP 2-4.5:** Intermediate greenhouse gas emissions trajectory.
- **SSP 3-7.0:** Medium-to-high emissions baseline trajectory.
- **SSP 5-8.5:** High-end emissions fossil-fueled development trajectory.

CMIP6 climate projections provide monthly temperature and precipitation projections across global climate models (GCMs) at native grid resolutions (typically 100–250 km).

WISE-APP employs the standard **delta method** to perturb historical ERA5-Land baseline observations using the projected monthly change fields from each CMIP6 model. This approach preserves the fine-scale spatial and temporal variability of historical observations while shifting the distribution according to projected climate trajectories across ensemble models.

## Directory Structure

```
data/
├── metadata/
│   ├── survey_list.csv
│   ├── variable_list.csv
│   └── cpi_ppp.csv
│
├── microdata/
│   ├── hh/{code}/
│   ├── ind/{code}/
│   ├── firm/{code}/
│   └── h3/{code}/
│
└── hazard/
    ├── weather/
    │   ├── historical/{code}/
    │   └── projections/{code}/
    └── events/
        ├── historical/{code}/
        └── probabilistic/{code}/
```

`{code}` is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (e.g., `GNB`, `NGA`, `ETH`).

## Metadata

Three CSV files are loaded when WISE-APP initializes. They drive UI filtering, variable labeling, and monetary conversions.

### `survey_list.csv`

Catalogs every survey round and observation level available in the microdata repository:

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `economy` | string | Economy / country name |
| `code` | string | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code |
| `year` | integer | Survey implementation year |
| `survname` | string | Survey acronym (e.g., `EHCVM`, `LSMS`, `HIES`) |
| `level` | string | Unit of observation: `hh` (household), `ind` (individual), or `firm` |
| `obs` | integer | Total number of observations |
| `source` | string | Harmonization source (e.g., `GMD`) |

### `variable_list.csv`

Catalogs all microdata variables and specifies their role and treatment in the modeling interface:

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Variable name in microdata files |
| `label` | string | Human-readable label displayed in the UI |
| `type` | string | Data type: `numeric`, `integer`, `logical`, `factor`, `character`, `Date` |
| `units` | string | Unit of measurement (e.g., `LCU/day`, `years`, `mm`) |
| `id` | binary | 1 if identifier, date, or administrative variable |
| `outcome` | binary | 1 if variable can serve as a dependent welfare outcome |
| `hazard` | binary | 1 if weather or climate hazard metric |
| `ind` | binary | 1 if available in individual-level data |
| `hh` | binary | 1 if available in household-level data |
| `firm` | binary | 1 if available in firm-level data |
| `area` | binary | 1 if measured at the geographic/community level |
| `interact` | binary | 1 if available as a policy/resilience interaction term |
| `fe` | binary | 1 if available as a fixed effect in regression models |

### `cpi_ppp.csv`

Provides deflators and purchasing power parity (PPP) conversion factors to convert monetary aggregates from nominal local currency units (LCU) to constant 2021 PPP USD:

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code |
| `year` | integer | Survey year |
| `data_level` | string | Geographic level of price index (e.g., `national`, `urban`, `rural`) |
| `cpi` | numeric | Consumer Price Index deflator |
| `ppp2021` | numeric | 2021 PPP conversion factor relative to USD |

## Microdata

Microdata files are stored in Apache Parquet format under `microdata/{level}/{code}/` following the naming convention `{code}_{year}_{survname}_{source}_{level}.parquet`:

```
microdata/hh/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_hh.parquet
microdata/ind/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_ind.parquet
microdata/firm/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_firm.parquet
microdata/h3/GNB/GNB_2018_EHCVM_GMD_h3.parquet
```

All microdata files share standard identifiers: `code`, `economy`, `year`, `survname`, `int_year`, `int_month`, `loc_id`, plus relevant thematic attributes.

### Household file (`_hh.parquet`)

One row per surveyed household. Key columns include:

- `hhid`: Unique household identifier within the survey.
- `welfare`: Household welfare measure (consumption or income in LCU/day, converted to 2021 PPP USD in modeling).
- `hhsize`: Number of household members.
- `loc_id`: Unique location code linking to the spatial H3 lookup.
- Resilience and asset indicators: electricity access, water source, dwelling characteristics, education of household head, etc.

### Individual file (`_ind.parquet`)

One row per individual member. Key columns include `hhid`, `pid` (person identifier), `wage` (earnings in LCU/day), `age`, `gender`, `education`, `employment_status`, and `loc_id`.

### Firm file (`_firm.parquet`)

One row per enterprise. Key columns include `fid` (firm identifier), `revenue` (daily revenue in LCU/day), `employees`, `sector`, and `loc_id`.

### H3 Spatial Lookup file (`_h3.parquet`)

Maps survey clusters (`loc_id`) to H3 hexagonal cells. A single lookup file covers all microdata levels from the same survey:

- Required columns: `code`, `year`, `survname`, `loc_id`, and `h3` (hexadecimal H3 index string).
- Optional column: `pop_2020` (GHS-POP 2020 population count), used to weight weather aggregations when a survey cluster spans multiple H3 cells.

## Hazard Data

Hazard datasets are stored in Parquet format, spatially indexed by H3 hexagon cells and temporally indexed at monthly resolution to align with microdata interview dates (`timestamp`, formatted as the first day of the month).

### Historical Weather

Stored under `hazard/weather/historical/{code}/{code}_{source}.parquet` (e.g., `GNB_era5land.parquet`).

Key variables include:

- `t`: Monthly mean temperature (°C).
- `tx`: Monthly mean of daily maximum temperatures (°C).
- `tp`: Total monthly precipitation (mm).
- `spei1`, `spei3`, `spei6`, `spei12`: Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index at 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month horizons.

### Climate Projections

Stored under `hazard/weather/projections/{code}/{code}_{source}_{scenario}.parquet`:

```
GNB_cmip6_historical.parquet   # CMIP6 historical baseline (1950–2014)
GNB_cmip6_ssp245.parquet       # CMIP6 SSP 2-4.5 (2015–2100)
GNB_cmip6_ssp370.parquet       # CMIP6 SSP 3-7.0 (2015–2100)
GNB_cmip6_ssp585.parquet       # CMIP6 SSP 5-8.5 (2015–2100)
```

In projection files, an additional `model` column identifies each climate model within the CMIP6 ensemble.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### Extreme Events (Future Release)
Modules for historical and probabilistic extreme events (e.g., riverine floods, tropical cyclone return periods) are planned for future releases of WISE-APP.
:::

## Spatial Integration: H3

WISE-APP links household survey microdata and gridded climate datasets using Uber's [H3 Spatial Index](https://h3geo.org), an open-source discrete global grid system based on hexagonal partitions:

- **Point / Cluster Geocoding:** Household survey sampling clusters (`loc_id`) are mapped to one or more H3 hexagons at the appropriate resolution.
- **Gridded Hazard Resampling:** Gridded weather datasets (ERA5-Land, CMIP6) are indexed onto the same H3 cell grid.
- **Flexible Joins Across Scales:** Multi-resolution spatial joins are handled efficiently via H3 parent–child hierarchical relationships.
